class.name: JRPGWindow
class.brief_description: A game window: a tinted back, a border, and contents inside a padding, opening and closing from its middle.
class.description: A window of the game's interface, such as a menu or a message box. It draws a back tinted by [member tone] and a nine-slice border over it, and lays its children out inside the padding, as [PanelContainer] does. [member openness] opens it from the middle: while it opens or closes, the frame is squashed into the band it opens through and the children show through that band only; closed, it draws nothing. Clicks land only on the part that shows; a closed window and its children take no clicks and keep no focus. [method open] and [method close] take [constant OPEN_FRAMES] frames at 60 frames a second and end with [signal opened] or [signal closed]. The skin comes from the theme items below, so a project theme or theme overrides replace it as for any control. Talewright's built-in skin is added to the default theme the first time a window needs it, so windows draw without any project file. Authority: client. Windows only show what the game decides.

method.name: close
method.description: Starts closing the window over [constant OPEN_FRAMES] frames; [signal closed] is emitted when it is closed. A window that is already closed emits it at once.

method.name: ensure_default_skin
method.description: Adds Talewright's built-in skin to the default theme, under the [code skip-lint]JRPGWindow[/code] theme type, unless it is there already. Windows call it before reading their theme items.

method.name: get_arrows_texture
method.description: Returns the skin's sheet of marks: four 16 by 16 marks side by side (scroll up, scroll down, pause, submenu).

method.name: get_back_texture
method.description: Returns the back as it is drawn: the skin's back with [member tone] added, or the skin's own back when the tone is zero.

method.name: get_content_rect
method.description: Returns the rectangle the contents go in: the window's rectangle inside the [theme_item padding], in the window's own coordinates.

method.name: get_cursor_texture
method.description: Returns the skin's selection cursor, a nine-slice image, for windows that draw their own contents.

method.name: get_icon_region
method.description: Returns the region of icon [param index] in [theme_item icon_set]: icon n is at column n modulo the icons a row holds, row n divided by them. Returns an empty rectangle when the set has no such icon.

method.name: get_icon_set_texture
method.description: Returns the icon set the window draws icons from ([theme_item icon_set]).

method.name: get_icon_size
method.description: Returns the size of one icon of the icon set, in pixels ([theme_item icon_size]).

method.name: get_last_sound
method.description: Returns the interface sound played last, a [enum JRPGSystemData.Sound] value, or [code]-1[/code]. It is recorded even when the System data has no sound for it.

method.name: get_open_rect
method.description: Returns the rectangle the window shows now: all of it when open, the band through its middle while it opens or closes.

method.name: get_sound_player
method.description: Returns the internal player of the interface sounds, made with the first sound played; [code]null[/code] before.

method.name: is_closing
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while the window is closing.

method.name: is_opening
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while the window is opening.

method.name: open
method.description: Starts opening the window over [constant OPEN_FRAMES] frames; [signal opened] is emitted when it is open. A window that is already open emits it at once.

method.name: play_sound
method.description: Plays one of the System data's interface sounds (cursor, OK, cancel, buzzer); silent when the database has none for it.

members.member: The database whose System data gives the interface sounds. If [code]null[/code], the project's database is used.
If [code]true[/code], the back and the border are drawn. Message windows on a dimmed or transparent background draw neither.
How open the window is, from 0 (closed, nothing drawn) to 1 (open). Setting it shows the window at once and stops any opening or closing, without a signal.
If [code]true[/code], the pause mark shows at the bottom middle while the window is open (a message waiting for the player). It takes the place of the scroll down mark.
If [code]true[/code], the scroll down mark shows at the bottom middle while the window is open.
If [code]true[/code], the scroll up mark shows at the top middle while the window is open.
Added to every pixel of the back, per channel, from -255 to 255, as the System data's window tone. The border and the contents keep their colors.

signal.name: closed
signal.description: Emitted when the window has finished closing.

signal.name: opened
signal.description: Emitted when the window has finished opening.

constants.constant: Frames, at 60 frames a second, that opening or closing takes.
The size of each mark in [theme_item arrows].

theme_items.theme_item: The margins of the [theme_item back] and [theme_item border] nine-slices, in pixels: corners keep their size, edges and the middle stretch.
The size of one icon of [theme_item icon_set], in pixels.
Space between the window's edge and its contents, in pixels.
Four marks side by side, [constant ARROW_SIZE] pixels each: scroll up, scroll down, pause, submenu.
The window's body, a nine-slice image drawn under the border and tinted by [member tone].
The window's border, a nine-slice image drawn over the back.
The selection cursor of lists, a nine-slice image.
The icon set: square icons of [theme_item icon_size] pixels in rows, an entry's icon index counting from the top left, row by row. Talewright's built-in set holds 16 icons a row.
